req.title: Redirect once when n==1
req.statement: The system shall respond with a single 302 to /get when /redirect/1 is called.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /redirect/1 must issue exactly one 302 redirect to /get, and the final response (after following the redirect) must be HTTP 200 with the expected JSON payload. We need: (1) a positive test confirming the 302 → /get chain works correctly with exact status codes and Location header; (2) a negative test confirming that /redirect/0 is rejected (assert=n>0 triggers 500 or 400, not a silent redirect); (3) a boundary test at n=1 (the exact threshold where the code branches to url_for('view_get') instead of _redirect), plus a contrast at n=2 to confirm the branch is not taken. We also test the Location header value exactly to catch constant/string mutations, and verify the final 200 payload keys to catch mutations in view_get.

tests.name: test_redirect_1_issues_302_to_get_endpoint
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client with follow_redirects=False
Assert final status code is exactly 200
Assert response JSON contains keys: url, args, headers, origin
expected: JSON body has keys url, args, headers, origin
trace: R-HTTPBIN-022: single 302 to /get when /redirect/1 is called
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_1_issues_302_to_get_endpoint():
    r1 = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r1.status_code == 302
    location = r1.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert location.endswith('/get'), f'Expected Location ending in /get, got {location!r}'
    r2 = client.get('/get')
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    data = r2.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    assert 'url' in data
    assert 'args' in data
    assert 'headers' in data
    assert 'origin' in data

tests.name: test_redirect_1_boundary_exact_single_hop_not_chained
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
n=1 is the exact branch point in redirect_n_times
actions: Assert exactly one 302 with Location ending in /get
Assert 302 with Location NOT ending in /get (it chains to /redirect/1)
Confirm n=1 branch is distinct from n=2 branch
expected: Both return 302 but with different Location targets
trace: R-HTTPBIN-022: BVA at n=1 (threshold) vs n=2 (n+1 above threshold)
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_1_boundary_exact_single_hop_not_chained():
    r1 = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r1.status_code == 302
    loc1 = r1.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert loc1.endswith('/get'), f'n=1 should redirect to /get, got {loc1!r}'

    r2 = client.get('/redirect/2', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    loc2 = r2.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert not loc2.endswith('/get'), (
        f'n=2 should NOT redirect directly to /get, got {loc2!r}'
    )
    assert '/redirect/1' in loc2, (
        f'n=2 should chain to /redirect/1, got {loc2!r}'
    )

Assert no extra redirect-related keys present

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_1_full_chain_final_payload_structure():
    r = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=True)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    expected_keys = {'url', 'args', 'headers', 'origin'}
    assert set(data.keys()) == expected_keys, (
        f'Expected keys {expected_keys}, got {set(data.keys())}'
    )
    assert data['args'] == {}, f'Expected empty args, got {data["args"]}'

tests.name: test_redirect_1_absolute_false_gives_relative_location
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Assert status 302 and Location is relative (starts with '/', not 'http')
expected: absolute=true: Location starts with 'http' and ends with '/get'
trace: R-HTTPBIN-022: DT covering absolute=true/false branch in redirect_n_times
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_1_absolute_false_gives_relative_location():
    r1 = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r1.status_code == 302
    loc1 = r1.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert loc1 == '/get', f'Default should be relative /get, got {loc1!r}'

    r2 = client.get('/redirect/1?absolute=false', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    loc2 = r2.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert loc2 == '/get', f'absolute=false should give /get, got {loc2!r}'

    r3 = client.get('/redirect/1?absolute=true', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r3.status_code == 302
    loc3 = r3.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert loc3.startswith('http'), f'absolute=true should give absolute URL, got {loc3!r}'
    assert loc3.endswith('/get'), f'absolute=true should end with /get, got {loc3!r}'
